newsitem.title: USA: Hong Kong faces grim times, China dissident says.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong faces grim times, China dissident says.

text.p: Chinese human rights activist Harry Wu on Thursday predicted a grim future for Hong Kong, which reverts to Chinese rule at midnight on June 30, because he said China's leaders have a history of breaking their promises.
Wu said it was absolutely certain Beijing would break its promise and introduce repressive rule into the territory of 6.4 million people.

"Hong Kong is finished," he told Reuters in an interview. "Do you think a free capitalist system under totalitarianism can survive? And who promised not to change it? Deng Xiaopeng and the communists."
"Would you check their record to see whether they have kept their word and their promises?"
Wu, who spent 19 years in forced labour camps, also said China's leaders would not dismantle their huge forced camp system because they needed it to retain power.
He was re-arrested in 1995 by the Chinese government when he tried to re-enter the country. Wu was freed after an international campaign waged on his behalf.
"It doesn't matter, Mao or Deng or the next leader -- if they maintain a totalitarian system, they need (forced labour camps)," he said.

Wu said there were still millions of dissidents in China, even though many have fled the country. He said the dissident movement included not just student leaders, but a vast underground network of religions, ethnic minorities, workers and peasants.
He said it was irrelevant whether students or intellectuals were dissidents, because China's history showed that meaningful change occured only when the workers and peasants were involved.
Wu, 60, also said he was deeply ashamed of some U.S. politicians who offered praise for Deng Xiaopeng, China's paramount leader who died last month.

Deng was in charge when the government waged a bloody crackdown on the 1989 student-led democracy movement in Beijing's Tiananmen Square, yet he also opened the doors to western investment and technology after taking power in 1979.
"I'm very embarrassed at some American politicians applauding a Chinese communist butcher," he said.
